author: Mark Atwood
text:
Same workspace-architectural family as .2/.3/.4/.10 — fix requires adding a new typed atomic method to ChatBackend (read_and_maybe_burn or similar) that performs the readAt write and the hard-delete in a single transaction. Alternative: handler-side reorder (expire first, then skip the readAt write) — but that requires backend cooperation to surface as 'destroyed' rather than 'updated' in the change log.

Recommendation: Path A (new typed method on ChatBackend) for the same reasons as .2 — backend is canonical for atomicity, downstream consumers can use their native storage primitives (PG transaction, FoundationDB transaction, etc.), and the reference MemoryBackend implements it under a single mutex acquisition. Default impl: returns 'not supported' so backends MUST opt in, OR falls back to the legacy split-call path with the documented gap.

Adding dependency on JMAP-x2gd.2 (the closest architectural sibling — also requires an atomic typed method) so .6 stays off the ready frontier until the family decision lands. Not labeling .6 as human — the architectural decision lives on .2.
